summary: North's 3-strut all-around freeride kite with unparalleled versatility and wind range. Lively and playful with easy jumps, upwind performance, and effortless relaunch. A true one-kite quiver solution.

The best foil-specific kite from North. Smooth power delivery and excellent drift for foil riding.

structured_review.summary: The 2025 North Reach is a genuinely refined all-around kite that earns its 'desert island' reputation by doing almost everything well — stable overhead, strong upwind, improved low-end grunt and better hang time than its predecessor. It won't out-loop a dedicated big-air kite or drift like a true wave kite, but for the vast majority of riders it covers every discipline competently. The bar feel improvements are the standout upgrade, giving clear kite position feedback without becoming twitchy.
pros: Significantly improved bar feel — clear, direct feedback without being overly reactive
Better low-end and top-end power range over the previous version
Strong upwind performance even in gusty conditions
Improved lift and hang time for jumping versus prior iteration
Genuinely versatile: works well on twin-tip, surfboard, and foil
Very stable overhead — parks confidently in gusty, punchy wind
cons: Not a dedicated big-air machine — jump height trails kites like the Orbit or XR
No real looping behavior compared to freestyle-oriented kites
Won't drift or go slack-line like a proper wave kite
Jack-of-all-trades ceiling means top specialists will outperform it in every specific discipline
structured_review.best_for: Riders who want a single quiver kite across twin-tip, foil, and occasional waves without chasing top-end performance in any one discipline.
structured_review.not_for: Riders who prioritize kite loops, maximum jump height, or true wave-riding drift — there are better purpose-built options.
structured_review.rec_blurb: The kite for 90% of kiters — refined, stable, and genuinely does it all.
